changes: Added a learning_scan CLI that derives finding-signals through the store ports and persists them to .lattice/learning/finding-signals.json — the cache the Phase 1.5 hint loader reads. This activates the previously-inert advisory review hints (no command wrote that cache before). Reuses the existing deriveFindingSignalsFromStore + writeFindingSignals machinery (finding-signals.ts / learning-store.ts unchanged); the only write is the materialHash-excluded learning cache. Registered as an L2 experience-layer (cache-writing, NOT read-only) command across cli-engine/registry/config/command-policy/process-fact-levels; kept out of READ_ONLY_COMMANDS.
usage: Run `node bin/lattice.js learning_scan` to derive+persist the cache; `learning_scan '{"json":true}'` for machine-readable output; `learning_scan '{"story":"<id>"}'` to restrict to one story.
expectedOutcome: The scan derives the finding-signals, writes .lattice/learning/finding-signals.json, and prints a summary; afterward advisory review hints can fire (they were empty before).
actualTranscript: learning_scan derived 31 signal(s) and wrote the cache (schemaVersion 1); --json emits {written,path,signals,schemaVersion,updatedAt}; --story restricts derivation; the hermetic smoke proves the hint loader returns NO hints before the scan and NON-EMPTY hints (recurring>=1, advisory header) after — the loop activates. git status shows no tracked-source change (cache is materialHash-excluded). Full npm test passes incl. process-fact-contract.
outcomeDiff: Matches expected: the scan activates the hint loop end-to-end (empty before -> firing after).
limitations: The scan is a faithful snapshot of ALL derived signals; referential-staleness filtering is NOT applied here (it stays at read time via B-a2e3's revalidateSignals leaf). signatureTag auto-candidate capture (story 3.2), A/B hint-mode gating (3.3), and the effectiveness metric (3.4) are separate later stories. Activating hints does NOT by itself prove the Experience Layer makes development smarter.
pitfalls: learning_scan WRITES the advisory cache, so it is NOT read-only — it must stay out of READ_ONLY_COMMANDS and carry a non-readOnly command-policy ownershipClass, and it MUST be registered in PROCESS_FACT_LEVELS (the derive-source for the process-fact contract; omitting it fails the npm test process-fact-contract suite). The cache lives under .lattice/learning/ (materialHash-excluded) so it never perturbs a gate. The first REVIEW round surfaced 2 test-coverage findings (resolved); the degraded 3x1 review escalation was recorded per solo-operator policy.
